overview: Colombia is a country in the north-west of South America, and the only South American country with coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea. Its capital and largest city is Bogotá. Colombia won independence from Spain in the 1810s and is named after Christopher Columbus. It is one of the world's leading producers of coffee and emeralds.

geography.text: Three ranges of the Andes run north through western Colombia, with fertile valleys between them where most people live. To the east are the grassy plains of the Llanos and the Amazon rainforest. Colombia is one of the most biodiverse countries on Earth, with more kinds of birds than any other country.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot on the coasts and in the Amazon, but mild all year in the mountain cities of Bogotá and Medellín.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: More bird species than any other country, plus jaguars, spectacled bears and humpback whales off the Pacific coast.

history.text: Colombia was home to peoples such as the Muisca, whose gold-working inspired the legend of El Dorado. It was the heart of the Spanish colony of New Granada and won independence in 1819 under Simón Bolívar. Decades of conflict between the government, guerrillas, paramilitaries and drug cartels marked the late 1900s, and a peace deal with the FARC rebels was signed in 2016.

events.title: Peace deal
events.text: The government signs a peace agreement with the FARC.

government.text: Colombia is a presidential republic. The President is elected every four years for a single term. Congress has a Senate and a House of Representatives. In 2016 the government signed a peace deal with the FARC rebel group, ending more than 50 years of conflict, though other armed groups remain active.

economy.text: Colombia exports oil, coal, coffee, flowers and bananas. It is famous for its coffee and is the second-largest exporter of cut flowers in the world. Tourism has grown fast since the peace deal.

culture.text: Colombia is home to the novelist Gabriel García Márquez, who won the Nobel Prize in 1982, and to musicians such as Shakira and Karol G. Cumbia and vallenato music come from its Caribbean coast. It is one of the most biodiverse countries on Earth, with more bird species than any other.

items.title: Gabriel García Márquez
items.text: His novel One Hundred Years of Solitude made magic realism famous.

items.title: Cartagena
items.text: A walled colonial port on the Caribbean.

items.title: Birds
items.text: Colombia has recorded more than 1,900 bird species.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Arepas, corn cakes, and bandeja paisa, a huge plate of beans, rice, meat and egg.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Cumbia and vallenato music, reggaeton stars, and the novels of García Márquez.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: The Barranquilla Carnival, listed by UNESCO, is one of the biggest in the world.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and Colombia won the Copa América in 2001. Cycling is a passion: Egan Bernal became the first Latin American to win the Tour de France in 2019. The country has also won Olympic gold in weightlifting and BMX.
